questions: Did this eye swelling and bruising begin after an injury or blow to the face or head?
Do you have eye pain, especially pain when moving the affected eye?
Has your vision in that eye become blurred, doubled, or reduced?
Have you had fever or felt acutely unwell?
Is the affected eye bulging forward or difficult to move?
Are you taking blood thinners or do you have a bleeding disorder?
Did the swelling begin suddenly over minutes to hours?
Have you recently had a sinus infection, dental infection, or skin infection near the eye?
Have you noticed easy bruising or bleeding elsewhere on your body?
Have you had recurrent nosebleeds, bleeding gums, or unusually heavy menstrual bleeding?
Have you recently started or changed any medication or supplement, including aspirin, ibuprofen, steroids, or herbal products?
Have you had unexplained weight loss, persistent fatigue, night sweats, or bone pain?
Have you noticed swelling of your legs, foamy urine, or shortness of breath?
Have you had recurrent episodes of similar spontaneous bruising around the eyes?
Do you have a history of a blood disorder, liver disease, kidney disease, or cancer?
Have you had severe coughing, vomiting, straining, or repeated sneezing shortly before the bruising appeared?
Is your known blood disorder, cancer, or other medical condition multiple myeloma, MGUS, or AL (light-chain) amyloidosis?
Have you ever been diagnosed with a monoclonal protein or abnormal plasma cells?
Have you had heart failure, an enlarged tongue, numbness or tingling in your hands or feet, or unexplained low blood pressure when standing?
Is the newly changed medication a corticosteroid, anticoagulant, antiplatelet drug, or chemotherapy/immunotherapy?
Have you had prolonged bleeding after surgery, dental work, or minor cuts despite a normal platelet count?
Is the newly changed medication an anticoagulant such as warfarin, apixaban, rivaroxaban, dabigatran, or heparin?
Is it an antiplatelet drug such as aspirin, clopidogrel, or ticagrelor?
Is it a corticosteroid taken by mouth or injection rather than a cream or inhaler?
Did the periorbital bruising and increased bruising begin after starting or increasing that medication?
Have you stopped the medication since the bruising began?
Have you had black stools, blood in your urine, vomiting of blood, severe headache, or any other significant bleeding?
Is the newly changed medication an SSRI or SNRI antidepressant?
Is it a nonsteroidal anti-inflammatory drug such as ibuprofen or naproxen?
Is the significant bleeding gastrointestinal bleeding, such as black or bloody stools?
Are the bruises painful before they appear?
Do the bruises tend to occur during periods of emotional stress?
Have coagulation tests ever been abnormal in the past?
Is the newly changed medication an antihypertensive, especially amlodipine or another calcium-channel blocker?
Is it an anti-seizure medication, antibiotic, or herbal supplement?
Did the significant bleeding consist only of easy skin bruising and the periorbital discoloration?
Have you had any bleeding from the nose, gums, vagina, rectum, urine, or lungs?
Have you had episodes of sudden facial swelling, hives, wheezing, or abdominal pain since starting the medication?
Do you have markedly stretchy skin, unusually flexible joints, or a history of poor wound healing?
orders: Complete blood count with platelet count and peripheral blood smear
Prothrombin time/INR and activated partial thromboplastin time
Comprehensive metabolic panel including liver enzymes, creatinine, and serum albumin
Urinalysis with urine protein quantification
Serum and urine protein electrophoresis with immunofixation and serum free light-chain assay
ECG and NT-proBNP level
Urgent prothrombin time/INR and activated partial thromboplastin time
Fibrinogen and thrombin time
Mixing study on any prolonged PT or aPTT
Factor VIII activity and factor VIII inhibitor (Bethesda assay)
von Willebrand factor antigen, von Willebrand factor activity, and factor VIII level
Urgent assessment for active internal bleeding, including fecal occult blood testing and CT head without contrast if the severe headache is present or there is any neurologic symptom
Repeat PT/INR, aPTT, fibrinogen, and thrombin time
Serum protein electrophoresis and immunofixation
Urine protein electrophoresis and immunofixation
Serum free κ and λ light-chain assay with ratio
Punch biopsy of affected periorbital skin with Congo-red staining and amyloid typing by mass spectrometry
Platelet function analysis (PFA-100/200 closure times) and platelet aggregation studies
Factor XIII activity assay
Serum cortisol level and, if low, ACTH stimulation test
Direct inspection of the mouth, skin, and scalp for additional purpura or mucosal bleeding
Ophthalmic examination including visual acuity, intraocular pressure, slit-lamp examination, and dilated fundus examination
